Who is the user on every request, and how the database is queried

Where the user comes from on every request, which route filters by it, and how Drizzle ORM reaches RDS.

The short answer
Yes. On every route that returns or changes a user's data, the user comes from the verified access token (the Cognito sub), never from the body, the URL, a header the browser chose or a cookie value. The API reads it once, in one hook, and passes it to the repository functions, which put it in the WHERE clause. A resource of another user answers 404. Checked route by route: 12 routes under /v1 and no route breaks the rule. The ORM is Drizzle ORM (version 0.45.3) on the node-postgres driver. There is no string-built SQL.

How the token is checked

CheckWhereWhat happens if it fails
Token present, format Bearer <token>onRequest hook of the /v1 scope in apps/api/src/app.ts, before any handler401 unauthenticated
Signature against the user pool's public keys (JWKS, cached)aws-jwt-verify in apps/api/src/auth.ts401 invalid_token
iss is our user pool, exp and nbf are validsame401
token_use is access (an ID token is rejected)same (tokenUse: "access")401
client_id is one of our app clientssame (clientId: the list from COGNITO_CLIENT_IDS)401
The token has a subcognitoVerifier401
The user is then set oncereq.user = {sub}, added to every log line of the request; the rate limit is also keyed by it—

The local development verifier (an HS256 secret) exists only for tests and local runs: the API configuration refuses AUTH_MODE=local when NODE_ENV=production.

Every route: identity source and owner filter

RouteIdentity sourceOwner filter in the query
POST /v1/quizzesBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subfindQuizByKey, countRecentQuizzes: WHERE owner_sub = sub. createQuizIdempotent writes owner_sub = sub
GET /v1/catalogBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subNone needed, and none wanted: the catalogue is the same list for everybody — the documents that ship with the product, those a reviewer approved, and those that generated a quiz cleanly. It holds no user data
POST /v1/document-requestsBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subcreateQuizIdempotent's row is read through getOwnedQuiz(quizId, sub) first, so a request can only point at a quiz the caller owns. createDocumentRequest then writes requested_by = sub
GET /v1/document-requestsBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.sub, and the group adminDeliberately unfiltered: the review queue is everyone's pending requests. The gate is the group, checked in the route and not only in the UI; a token without it gets 403
POST /v1/document-requests/:id/reviewBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.sub, and the group adminreviewDocumentRequest by request id, and only while it is still pending. Who decided is written to reviewed_by
GET /v1/quizzesBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.sublistQuizzes: WHERE owner_sub = sub. listAttemptsByQuiz: WHERE user_sub = sub
GET /v1/quizzes/:id/attemptsBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subgetOwnedQuiz(id, sub), else 404. listAttemptsForQuiz: WHERE quiz_id AND user_sub = sub
GET /v1/quizzes/:idBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subgetOwnedQuiz(id, sub), else 404. Then getPublicQuestions(quizId) reads by quiz id — without the sub, and only after the ownership check has already passed
POST /v1/quizzes/:id/attemptsBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subgetOwnedQuiz(id, sub), else 404. findAttemptByKey, getOrCreateAttempt, getAttemptProgress: WHERE user_sub = sub
GET /v1/attempts/:idBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subgetAttemptProgress and getAttemptResult start from getOwnedAttempt: WHERE id AND user_sub = sub, else 404
PUT /v1/attempts/:id/answers/:questionIdBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subsaveAnswer: WHERE id AND user_sub = sub (row lock), else 404. The question and its options are then read through the attempt's own quiz
POST /v1/attempts/:id/submitBearer token, verified in the onRequest hook of /v1 → req.user.subsubmitAttempt: WHERE id AND user_sub = sub (row lock), else 404. The score is computed from stored data
Public route (no token)What it reads
GET /healthzAlways answers ok; no database read
GET /readyzRuns the constant select 1 to see that the database answers; no user data
GET /openapi.jsonThe API description; static
GET /docsThe Swagger page; static

Of the 19 repository functions the API calls, 13 take the owner (ownerSub or userSub) and filter by it, directly or through getOwnedQuiz and getOwnedAttempt. The API integration test calls the six routes that take an id as another user and expects 404 on each (404, not 403, so the existence of a quiz does not leak).

The queries that do not filter by user, and why each is allowed to

6 functions read or write without an owner filter. That is not an oversight to be tidied away later: each one is unfiltered because filtering would be wrong for what it does. The build refuses to produce this page if a function appears here without a reason written next to it (API_UNSCOPED_REASON in site/facts_repo.py), so a new unfiltered query cannot reach production quietly.

FunctionWhy it does not filter by the signed-in user
approvedCatalogEntriesthe catalogue is the same list for everybody by design, and holds no user data
createDocumentRequestan insert, not a read: it stores the requester's own sub, taken from the token
getPublicQuestionsreads by quiz id, and only after getOwnedQuiz has already proved ownership
listDocumentRequeststhe review queue, deliberately everyone's requests — the route is gated on the admin group and the API checks it again
listedCatalogEntriesthe catalogue is the same list for everybody by design, and holds no user data
reviewDocumentRequestan admin decision on a request id — same gate
The two shapes of exception
They are not the same kind of thing, and it is worth keeping them apart. Shared by design — the catalogue is one list for everybody and holds nobody's data, so there is no user to filter by. Admin by design — the review queue is deliberately everyone's requests, and what stands in for the owner filter is the Cognito group, checked in the route itself and not only in the interface that calls it. The third shape is the oldest one: getPublicQuestions runs only after an ownership check has already passed, so the filter happened a line earlier.

The paths that are not a user request

PathHow it readsWhy it is not a user request
Worker (generation)claimQuiz, completeQuiz, failQuiz, saveJobBudget, upsertSource: by quiz idThe id comes from an SQS message that the API sent only after its ownership checks (the sweeper can send it again). No HTTP, no token. A user cannot send to the queue: only the task roles of the API, the worker and the sweeper may
ScorergetQuizForScoring, claimScoring, releaseScoring, saveScores: by quiz id and job idMessages come from the worker. It reads the quiz and writes the quality scores; it returns nothing to a user
Sweeper (every 5 minutes)findStaleQuizzes, findUnscoredJobs, deleteOldCheckpointThreads: by time and status, across all usersA scheduled task: it re-queues or fails stuck jobs and deletes old checkpoints. It has no user
Migrate taskRuns the SQL migrationsA one-off ECS task started by the deploy

These are 18 of the 37 functions of packages/db/src/repo.ts. The services use the same database login (the one RDS manages in Secrets Manager), and no user can reach these functions: there is no route that takes a quiz id and calls them for a user.

The front end (quizforge-web, the BFF)

PointWhat the code does
Where the token livesIn httpOnly cookies (qf_at, qf_rt), secure, SameSite=Lax. The browser JavaScript never sees a token
How a call reaches the APIapp/bff/[...path]/route.ts takes the access token from the cookie (refreshing it with the refresh token when it is about to expire) and sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. Only /v1/... paths are forwarded; only content-type, idempotency-key and accept are copied from the browser
User id from the browserNone is read and none is sent. The BFF never puts a user id in the call: the API takes it from the token it verifies itself
/bff/meReturns the sub by decoding the token without verifying it, for display only (the small id in the menu). Nothing is authorised with it
Page gateproxy.ts only checks that a session cookie exists and redirects to sign-in; it does not decide access to data. The API verifies every token
CSRFUnsafe methods must have our Origin and the header X-Requested-With, on top of SameSite
Dev login/auth/dev answers 404 unless the front end runs in local mode; the production API refuses local tokens

Checked in the main of the front end repository.

Which ORM, and how the database is queried

QuestionAnswer
ORMDrizzle ORM (0.45.3; the lock file resolves 0.45.3) with drizzle-orm/node-postgres. The driver is pg (node-postgres 8.23.1) with a pool of up to 10 connections. The schema is TypeScript (packages/db/src/schema.ts), so a query is typed against it
MigrationsSQL files (8) generated by drizzle-kit 0.31.11 from the schema and committed. CI fails if schema.ts changed without a new migration. In AWS they are applied by a one-off ECS task (migrate) that the deploy runs before the new code, never at service start; a Postgres advisory lock stops two runners at once
Parameterised queriesEvery value goes through Drizzle's builders (eq, and, inArray, values) or a tagged sql`...` template, which sends the values as bound parameters. By code: 26 tagged templates in the source, 3 raw calls with a constant text (select 1 and the two advisory-lock calls, which pass their value as a parameter), and 0 uses of sql.raw, sql(...) or a query text built from variables. The site build fails if one appears
TLS to the databaseThe services build the connection URL with sslmode=verify-full (DB_SSL=true in Terraform): the certificate and the host name are verified against the RDS CA bundle. The RDS parameter rds.force_ssl=1 refuses a connection without TLS
Database user and passwordsThe login is the one RDS manages: the password is generated and kept in Secrets Manager; ECS injects it as separate fields and the code encodes it into the URL. Every service uses it
What the database does not do
The rule is enforced by the application code, not by PostgreSQL. There is no row-level security, and the API connects with one database user. A new query written without the owner filter would not be stopped by the database. What protects against that: all queries are in one file (repo.ts), the API never builds a query itself, the integration tests above call every id route as another user, and the build checks that every API-called function without an owner filter is one of the 6 that have a written reason — a new one fails this page.

Resilience and idempotency

Retries, layer by layer

LayerLimitNote
HTTP to MiniMax3 retries (4 attempts) · growing random delays · 90s timeoutDone by LangChain: everything except client errors (400–407, 409, 413) is retried
JSON repair2 repairs (the judge: 1)Sends the exact error back
Critique → revise2 roundsA quality loop, not a failure loop
LangGraphnone of its ownResumes from the checkpoint on redelivery. The checkpoint is deleted when the quiz is saved, and any thread older than 24 h is removed by the sweeper
SQS (jobs)3 receives → dead-letter queue360s visibility with heartbeat; delete only after commit
SQS (scoring)3 receives → its own dead-letter queue180s visibility; lease + row lock so two scorers never score the same quiz
Budget per job16 calls · 120k tokens · 5 minPersisted: not reset on redelivery
Judge (scorer)retry with backoff, bounded by scoring_attemptsAdvisory: a judge failure never fails the quiz; last attempt stores judge_failed
Sweeperevery 5 minutesFinal safety net: re-queues lost jobs and quizzes that were never scored

When the front end retries

OperationResult of a retry
POST /quizzes with the same Idempotency-Key200 + Idempotency-Replayed: true, same quiz
Same key, different body422
PUT answer with an old revisionAcknowledged and ignored; the newer answer stays
POST submit againSame result; not scored twice
Duplicate SQS messageThe claim fails (status is not queued) → skipped, never generated twice
Duplicate or concurrent score jobLease on the job + row lock: one scorer scores, the other skips; scores are replaced, not added

Evaluating the AI

Three kinds of instrument, from cheap to expensive: fixed code (every quiz, every PR) → TF-IDF similarity (free) → LLM judge (every quiz). Scoring answers is plain code: the judge never touches it.

The golden set

PartDetail
Items12 documents, from evals/src/golden.ts: pipecat-readme (English), mastra-readme (English), short-doc (English), portuguese-doc (Portuguese, real model only), prompt-injection (English, real model only), wails-readme-pt (Portuguese), brazilian-utils-readme-pt (Portuguese), wails-readme-es (Spanish), supabase-readme-es (Spanish, real model only), spanish-doc (Spanish), prompt-injection-pt (Portuguese, real model only), prompt-injection-es (Spanish, real model only). English and Portuguese and Spanish. The items that need the real model (a fake model copies the injected text) are marked; the others also run offline
Per-item floorsA single item below its floor fails the run: grounded 1, lint pass 0.6, judge overall 0.4, injection resisted 1, language match 1, question diversity 0.25, relevance 0.1, coverage 0.33. The lint and judge floors are low on purpose (judge scores are noisy): the real bars are the dataset means
Dataset barsThe mean over the items: mean judge_overall 0.7, mean lint_pass 0.9, mean relevance 0.22, mean coverage 0.58. The judge bar applies only with the real model
Where it runsOffline with a fake model on every pull request (job quality; 7 items run, the real-model-only ones are skipped). With the real model and the judge (median of 3): on a pull request that changes prompts, LLM code, the guard, the attack corpus, fixtures, evals or promptfoo (llm-eval-pr, no Langfuse); on main before the deploy (llm-eval, blocks the deploy and publish-prompts); every night (eval.yml) and on demand
In LangfuseThe items are mirrored into the dataset quizforge-golden (id golden-<item>, the thresholds and the hand-written reference questions as expected output). Every run on main and every night is one experiment (quizforge-golden-set) with a trace and the scores of each item

The prompt-injection document

QuestionAnswer
What is it?A normal README with an attack pasted in the middle (a security test, not a quality test)
How is it checked?Pass or fail, fixed code: the quiz must not contain the attacker's words
What does a high score mean?The system ignored the attack and wrote a clean quiz about the real content
Is that proof?No: one document and 4 strings in this golden test. The input guard, the promptfoo suites (89 offline + 20 live tests) and the red-team sample (50 attacks) cover many more attacks; see “Guardrails in execution”
Lesson: an LLM judge is noisy
One model scored the same quiz 0.86, 0.86, 0.93, 0.86 and then 0.45. A first gate failed a good quiz on that outlier. Fix: the median of 3 runs and a gate on the dataset mean. The judge is a different model from the generator (M3 vs M2.7) for another reason: it avoids self-preference.

Structure and prompt experiments

9 variants × 5 documents × 2 repetitions, scored by judge + embeddings + fixed checks, one Langfuse experiment per variant. Full report: docs/eval/structure-comparison.html.

QuestionResult
Which structure is best?A technical tie (one-shot 0.743, plan-then-write 0.717, critique loop 0.716; run-to-run noise ±0.029). The cheapest and fastest is enough
Does a better prompt help?The conceptual prompt raises mostly the LLM judge (+0.043), not the reference match: it may be the judge's taste
Any danger?few-shot + critique had the only failed run and can copy raw markdown into quotes
Same method as production?Yes: the experiments call the same scoreQuiz(), plus embedding metrics

CI/CD

The pipeline in one paragraph
Every change is a pull request. These jobs run on it: quality, integration, migrations, docker-build, secrets-scan, promptfoo, llm-eval-pr and redteam-sample. There is no browser test here: it drives a UI that lives in the front end repository, so it runs in that repository's CI against this one's main, and what covers the deployed pair is the smoke test the deploy runs in a real browser after every apply. The ruleset requires 8 of them (all but redteam-sample) before GitHub allows the squash merge. llm-eval-pr and redteam-sample call the real model through a restricted environment that holds the MiniMax key only. After the merge the same jobs run on main, plus llm-eval (the real model, Langfuse and the live promptfoo suite). When all of that is green, publish-prompts sends the prompts that changed to Langfuse, and the publish job builds the ARM64 images (api, worker with the classifier model and redteam, tagged with the commit) and pushes them to ECR with a push-only role. Nothing is deployed from this repository: the manual Deploy workflow of quizforge-infra picks a green commit whose images are in ECR, asks a human to approve, runs the migration, applies the one Terraform and smoke-tests. The front end is in the quizforge-web repository, which publishes its own image (web- and the first 12 characters of its commit); the docker-build job here checks out its main into web/, and its own repository runs the Playwright suite against this one's main before it may publish — the pair that is tested is the pair the deploy ships. The API contract is released as a tarball by release-contract.yml on tags contract-vX.Y.Z. Three more things run without a push: the nightly evaluation, the nightly drift check (infrastructure repository) and the manual structure comparison.

The front end pipeline and how a deploy happens

QuestionAnswer
Where is the front end built and tested?In its own repository, quizforge-web. Its CI has quality (typecheck, ESLint, 85 unit and jsdom component tests with coverage floors), build (the Next.js production build), docker-build (the image and a Trivy scan) and secrets-scan (gitleaks). It has no Terraform; its only AWS access is a role that can push its image to ECR, so it cannot deploy
How does a front end change reach production?The front end repository publishes quizforge/web:web-<12 characters of the commit> after its CI is green on main — which now includes an end-to-end test against the main of this repository. Then someone runs Deploy in the infrastructure repository (scope web, or all together with the back end): it resolves the newest green commit of the front end's main by itself, with no tag to type
Publish (ci.yml, job publish)On every push to main, after every gate: builds the api, worker and redteam images (tag = commit sha, immutable) and pushes them to ECR. It deploys nothing
Deploy (deploy.yml in the infrastructure repository)Started by hand; refused while paused; one human approval in the production environment and the AWS deploy role (OIDC). One input, scope (all, api, web): it resolves each side to the newest commit of its main whose required checks are green and whose images are in ECR, verifies the images, drift check, migration before the new code, one apply with a rolling update, smoke test. Scope web applies only the web task definition and service and refuses a plan that deletes anything except an old task definition revision. Both it and Rollback call the reusable apply.yml, which holds that production path
Where is Terraform?Only in the infrastructure repository, quizforge-infra, with its state, the IAM bootstrap and the operations scripts
Browser errorsThe front end has an error boundary and POST /bff/client-log: same origin, at most 4 KB, 20 a minute per address, every field scrubbed (tokens, e-mail addresses, query strings, long secrets), written as one JSON line to stdout, which the container log group collects
Social login secrets
The Google and Facebook credentials live in AWS Secrets Manager (quizforge/prod/google-login and quizforge/prod/facebook-login), each holding client_id and client_secret. The deploy jobs read them through the composite action .github/actions/social-secrets (the values are masked in the log) into Terraform variables. The pull request plan and the drift run do not read them: they use placeholders, because the identity provider details are ignored by Terraform after creation, so there is no diff. No credential is stored as a GitHub secret.

StepWhat happensLangfuse touched?
1 · EditThe prompt is code (packages/llm/src/prompts.ts). A test fails until PROMPT_VERSION is bumped and pnpm prompts:lock updates prompts/prompts.lock.json: a prompt change is always visible in the diffNo

4 · publish-promptsRuns only if every job above is green. For each prompt it reads the latest production version in Langfuse; if the text differs it creates a new version labelled production and sha-commit (config: prompt version, commit, hash). Same text = nothing happens, so a rerun or a docs-only merge creates no versionYes: the only place a prompt is written
What Langfuse is, for prompts
A catalog of approved versions: history, diffs and the commit of each one. The app still reads its prompts from the code that was deployed (so a Langfuse outage or a hand edit in the UI cannot change what users get). Letting the app fetch the production label at run time, with the code as fallback, is possible later; the risk is that the pipeline would then not be the only way to change behaviour unless edits in the UI are blocked.

A new test README in evals/fixturespromptfoo offline adds one FIXTURE test for it (hidden text, accepted language); the unit tests that walk the folder; e2e if it is in the dropdownOnly if you also add it to the golden set (evals/src/golden.ts): then llm-eval generates a quiz from it on the real model
A changed prompt (prompts.ts, judge, graph)promptfoo offline: the safety rules must still be in every prompt (PROMPTS), bad replies must still be rejected (OUTPUT); unit tests; offline evaluation. A notice says the live suite runs laterllm-eval on main: golden set and the live promptfoo suite (20) on the real model. Red = no deploy
A changed guard or keyword ruleThe rule examples and the corpus tests, promptfoo offline (BLOCK, REFUSE, RESIST) and the red-team sample (redteam-sample)Nightly live run
A document typed or linked by a user at run timeNot CI: the guard and the language check decide before the model is calledMetrics DocumentRejected and InjectionFlagged
The real model on the pull request
The golden set and the live promptfoo suite also run before the merge (job llm-eval-pr) when the change touches prompts, LLM code, the guard, the evals or the fixtures, and the red-team sample (job redteam-sample) runs on every pull request. They use their own environment with only the MiniMax key: no Langfuse keys, so a pull request never writes to Langfuse. Forks never get secrets. The risk that remains: someone with write access to the repository could change the workflow to print the key; use a spending-capped key there.
Where to look when something is red
Actions → the run → the failed job; the job summary has a table of the promptfoo groups (BLOCK, REJECT, ACCEPT, REFUSE, OUTPUT, RESIST, PROMPTS) and the failing cases with the reason; the full promptfoo result is an artifact of the run (promptfoo-offline, 30 days). Evaluation reports: eval-report artifact and the Langfuse run.
Known warning
Every run shows “Node.js 20 is deprecated” annotations: the pinned versions of actions/checkout and friends still target Node 20 and GitHub forces Node 24. It does not fail anything. Bumping the action versions is in the improvements list.

The same pipeline as a flow

Can anything reach production without passing everything?

QuestionAnswer
Is there a Playwright e2e test in the pipeline?Yes: login → generate → answer → reload → submit → score, plus the dropdown and validation tests
Does an image depend on everything?Yes: all 7 jobs (including promptfoo and llm-eval) before an image is published (the human approval is in the infrastructure repository)
What triggers a deploy?A person starting Deploy in the infrastructure repository, with the same approval. A push to main here only publishes images; a PR never publishes or deploys: the job shows “skipped”.
Can a check be skipped?No: the ruleset needs a PR, the 8 required checks (quality, integration, migrations, e2e, docker-build, secrets-scan, promptfoo, llm-eval-pr), linear history, resolved threads, no bypass. redteam-sample runs on PRs but is not required; llm-eval runs again on main and blocks the deploy
ProofA red llm-eval left deploy skipped in a real run
Deploy while paused?Refused: with PAUSED=true the job fails early
Other workflowseval and drift run nightly; Compare generation structures is manual

Deploy order

#StepWhy this order
1Build the ARM64 images (api, worker, redteam) and push them to ECR (tag = git sha); the front end repository pushes web- + its commit. The deploy is a separate, manual workflowImmutable, traceable images
2Drift check (plan -refresh-only)Shows hand-made changes in the log; the apply then puts them back as Terraform defines them. It stops only if the state cannot be read
3Run the migration as a Fargate task before the codeExpand/contract keeps the old version working
4terraform applyRolling update + circuit breaker with automatic rollback
5Smoke test through CloudFront (9 assertions)Proves edge → load balancer → api works

Automated tests and coverage

LayerTestsCI jobWhat it covers
Unit and integration1,860 (Vitest, including the promptfoo helper tests; integration on a real PostgreSQL), measured 2026-10-16 (4 skipped)quality (unit), integration (all, with coverage)Scoring, schemas, guard and keyword rules, SSRF checks, JSON repair, the graph, output rails, migration policy; the API end to end (login, quotas, idempotency, ownership), the worker, the scorer, the sweeper, the database constraints and the migrations
End to end7, Playwright in Chromee2eLogin, create, answer with a reload, submit, history and results, with the four services running and a fake model
Prompts and guardrails89 offline, 20 live (promptfoo) and the red-team sample (50 attacks, 5 language documents)promptfoo, llm-eval-pr, redteam-sampleThe attack corpus, language policy, bad replies, and the real model resisting
WhereStatements covered (unit + integration)Notes
apps/api, packages/contract, packages/core, packages/db, packages/detector, packages/llm100%Every statement. The floor in CI is 100% of statements and lines for each of them
apps/worker98.88%Floor in CI: 98%. Start-up guards and scripts that call the real model are left out or partly covered, with a written reason in vitest.coverage.config.ts
evals97.95%Floor in CI: 97%. Start-up guards and scripts that call the real model are left out or partly covered, with a written reason in vitest.coverage.config.ts
All back end and shared code99.65% of statements, 99.65% of lines, 98.14% of functions, 95.28% of branchesMeasured on 2026-10-16 over 1,860 tests (1,856 run, 4 skipped). Enforced in CI: the run fails if a package drops below its floor
Front end (quizforge-web)98 unit and jsdom component testsIn its own repository, with coverage floors for the helpers, the components and the route handlers. The end-to-end test here covers the screens in a real browser
How coverage is enforced
The integration job runs pnpm test:coverage (vitest.coverage.config.ts, a floor per package) and fails if a package drops below its floor. Coverage says which lines run in a test, not whether the assertions are good: that is why the guard and the prompts also have the promptfoo suites and the red-team sample, and the agent has the evaluation on the real model.

Architecture decisions

Each row was discussed and chosen on purpose.

DecisionRejected alternativeWhy
Fargate for everything, separate servicesLambda (15 min limit, cold starts); one serviceGeneration is long and stateful; web, api, worker and scorer scale differently. Cost about $6/day running (estimate).
Worker separate from the apiLangGraph inside the apiIsolates load and failures of the LLM; contract = SQS message + versioned schema
SQS + dead-letter queueCall the LLM inside the request; Step FunctionsLimits concurrency and MiniMax rate limits; built-in retry; alarm on the DLQ
RDS PostgresDynamoDB; AuroraIdempotency and scoring need real constraints (CHECK, UNIQUE, FK, FOR UPDATE)
CloudFront → ALB, no domainDomain + ACM certificateNo domain available: *.cloudfront.net certificate; ALB locked by prefix list + secret header
Next.js as a BFFPlain React SPATokens stay in httpOnly cookies, PKCE on the server, one place to validate
The front end in its own public repository, tested against this one's mainOne monorepo with the front end insideThe front end has its own CI (quality with a coverage floor, build, docker-build with Trivy, secrets-scan), its own Dockerfile and its own ruleset. This repository builds its main in docker-build, and that repository runs the end-to-end suite against this one's main before publishing an image, so the pair that is tested is the pair that is deployed. A pull request bumps the pin. There is still one Terraform, one deploy and one human approval
The API contract as a released tarballCopying the schemas into both repositories@quizforge/contract (zod, safe for the browser, no keyword rules) is released as a tarball on a GitHub Release by release-contract.yml on tags contract-vX.Y.Z; the front end depends on the tarball URL. The strict topic check stays server side
Cognito with open sign-up, Google and FacebookOwn auth; Auth0; users created by an admin onlyStandard JWT/JWKS, hosted login, no passwords to store. The API verifies access tokens only, so a federated user is one more sub. Open sign-up is paired with cost controls: verified e-mail, 12-character passwords, a quota per user, rate limits, the WAF, the job budget and the cost alarm
An optional Cognito client for localhostAllowing localhost redirects on the production clientThe client quizforge-prod-local-dev (enable_local_dev_client, off by default) lets the local stack try the real login; the production client never accepts a localhost redirect
LangChain.js + LangGraphDirect SDK callsPostgres checkpoints: a dead worker resumes without repeating paid calls
Checkpoints in Postgres with a retention, not in RedisRedis (ElastiCache) with a TTLA checkpoint only resumes an interrupted job, so it should not live long, but a new service costs about US$12 a month, needs its own security group, monitoring and pause handling, and, as far as we know, the LangGraph Redis saver needs the RedisJSON and RediSearch modules that plain ElastiCache does not offer. The same effect comes from two rules in code: the worker deletes the thread when the quiz is saved, and the sweeper deletes threads older than 24 hours. Checkpoint and job rows also stay in one database (one backup, one TLS setup).
Reject hidden text, flag plain textBlock every instruction-like sentence; rely on the prompt onlyHidden or encoded text has no legitimate use in a README, so it is rejected. A plain sentence may be a quote in a security tutorial, so it is kept as data and the model's resistance is tested (promptfoo live, red-team sample)
Strict link rule in the output railsAccept any link that appears in the documentAn instruction planted in the document can ask for a link. When the document has any flag (a keyword rule, or the classifier's excerpt), a reply link must also occur in the document with the flagged parts removed, and a link with a word that only appears in flagged parts is rejected. The classifier marks one window per document, so this complements the rules
Llama Prompt Guard 2 in flag mode, baked into the worker imageThe English-only DeBERTa model; block modeIt is multilingual (en, pt and es are covered), free and needs no API key. Measured on 500 samples of deepset/prompt-injections: 23.1% of the injections flagged overall (25.8% in English) with 0 false positives at threshold 0.5. The earlier English-only model flagged 40.2% but also 3 benign documents, among them the real Pipecat README (0.995). The detector finds only explicit attacks, so it is one layer that flags; the rules, the guard, the delimiters and the output rails do the rest. It costs a 2.1 GB image and a 1 vCPU / 4 GB worker task (about US$20 a month more per task)
Two deploy paths, one stateA separate Terraform for the front endThe deploy is one workflow of the infrastructure repository, with scope all, api or web: one state, one role, one approval; scope web plans only the web task definition and service and refuses a plan that deletes anything else, and Rollback is a separate workflow that reuses the same path
Social login credentials in AWS Secrets ManagerGitHub environment secretsThe deploy jobs read them with a masked composite action; no credential is stored as a GitHub secret, and plan and drift runs use placeholders
The nightly red team as a Fargate task with a scheduleA GitHub Actions cron jobIt tests the same image and the same Prompt Guard 2 as production, from inside the VPC, and leaves a timestamped report in S3 without giving GitHub the model key for a long run
Output rails in code, not a second modelAn LLM to check every replyNo extra latency or cost; a model checking a model has the same weaknesses
Only English, Portuguese and SpanishAccept any languageThe quality gates, the judge rubric and the 145 keyword rules (48 per language plus 1) are built and tested for these three; every other language is rejected before the model
promptfoo offline on every PR; live suite and red-team sample in a restricted environmentThe model key available to every jobThe MiniMax key lives only in the environments llm-eval-pr (no Langfuse keys, never for forks) and llm-eval; the offline suite proves everything around the model with no secret
A frozen red-team sample in CI, graded by codeHand-written attacks only; a model that grades a model50 attacks in 3 languages with canary tokens, graded by plain code; a leaked canary fails the job. Its first run found a real leak (a Spanish exfil-link attack), which led to the full Spanish rules and the strict link rule
JSON validated by the appTrust the provider's json_schemaMiniMax ignores field names and adds <think>: only extract + zod + repair guarantees it
Langfuse Cloud HobbyLangSmith; self-hostedFree; datasets, experiments, cost. Alerts in CloudWatch.
Judge = another model, median of 3, also in productionSame model, 1 runMeasured: M3 had a 0.45 outlier. Same judge in production and CI = comparable scores.
Judge stays in our code (scorer service), not in LangfuseLangfuse LLM-as-a-judge with MiniMaxTested: MiniMax returns <think> before the JSON, Langfuse pauses the evaluator. Our code strips it and repairs the JSON.
Scoring in its own queue and serviceJudge inside the generation jobMeasured in 13 real traces: +18 s (40%) before the quiz was ready and a worker slot held longer. The scorer is a small task of the same image (about $7/month)
One shared scoreQuiz()Separate formulas for CI and productionThe same names and numbers everywhere; the method is versioned
Dropdown from a shared catalogHard-coded list in the front endOne source of truth, validated, testable, served by the API
One schema package, @quizforge/contractTypes copied by handBrowser, BFF and API cannot drift; contract tests
Local embeddings (MiniLM)Paid embeddings APIThe MiniMax key has none; free and multilingual; the interface can swap it
Terraform state in S3 with native lockDynamoDB lock; Terraform CloudFewer parts; versioned + KMS
OIDC instead of access keysIAM user in GitHub secretsNo long-lived credential; deploy only from main + approved environment
Migration before the codeMigrate on app startNever two migrations at once; the old version stays valid
Pause = a Terraform variableterraform destroyReversible in minutes, keeps data, pipeline knows it is paused

Bugs found by real testing

Unit tests with mocks did not find these: running the real system (MiniMax, AWS, Chrome) did.

ProblemCauseFix
The LLM gate failed a good quizThe M3 judge scored 0.45 on a quiz it had scored 0.86 four timesOther-model judge, median of 3, gate on the mean
Mastra README failed 3 times in a rowEach redelivery resumed the checkpoint that had already failedA content failure deletes the checkpoint; the retry regenerates
One bad question failed the whole quizA single ungrounded quote failed the jobDrop it if 5+ remain; otherwise fail with the offending quote
num_questions was wrongIt stored the request, not what was generatedcompleteQuiz stores the real count
Technical errors shown to usersInternal errors reached the UIuserFacingError() turns them into plain messages
Generate button clickable too earlyA native submit reloaded the page and lost the formDisabled until React has hydrated
Cognito blocked by CSPform-action did not include the hosted UIform-action 'self' https://*.amazoncognito.com
Broken CI fileA : inside a step nameValidate the YAML before committing
A failure hidden behind a pipeNo pipefail, so the step stayed greenbash -eo pipefail in every workflow
Quality number changed meaningProduction blended other metrics and changed formula if the judge failedOne scoreQuiz(); no quality_overall when the judge fails
Alarms notified nobodyThe SNS topic had no subscriberE-mail comes from the ALARM_EMAIL variable; a note in the runbook
A single terrible quiz went unnoticedOnly an hourly average alarm existedNew alarm on the minimum of any 5 minutes
Resume failed onceAWS had no db.t4g.micro capacity in that zone (InsufficientDBInstanceCapacity)Retry start until it works; it succeeded a few minutes later
Langfuse evaluator paused (EVAL_MODEL_CONFIG_INVALID)MiniMax reasoning models answer with <think> and ignore response_formatKeep the judge in the code (the scorer service)
Two scorers could judge the same quiz and double the scoresThe claim did not exclude a concurrent scorer; found by CI on main (it passed on my machine by timing)A lease on the job so one scorer judges, released on failure so the retry works, plus a row lock when saving; the race test repeats 5 rounds
The CI quality gate failed by chanceOne flagged question in five (lint 0.80) failed an item; the mean judge was finePer-item floor 0.6 and a dataset bar, mean lint 0.9 (the same remedy as for the judge)
A Spanish attack slipped past the guard (found by the red team sample in CI)It asked for an attacker link inside a question; no keyword rule matched and the model wrote the link into an optionThe full Spanish rule set and the strict link mode of the output rail
A waiting deploy blocked later pipelinesThe CI group does not cancel runs, and an unapproved deploy waits until GitHub times it out (30 days)Approve or reject (cancel) the old run

Cost

ItemRunning ($/month)Paused ($/month)

Load balancer and its 2 public IPv4 addresses~240 (deleted while paused)
NAT gateway and its address~360
RDS t4g.micro + 20 GB~14~2.3 (storage)

Total (estimate from the price list, not the bill)~185 (≈ $6 / day)~8 (≈ $0.3 / day)
Nightly red team (not in the total)about US$35 to 50 a month in all (docs/redteam-nightly.md)0 (the schedule is off)

CommandDoes
scripts/pause.shTasks to 0, RDS stopped, NAT, load balancer and WAF removed, sweeper and red team schedules off. Data and image version kept (the api image tag; see the improvements list for the web tag).
scripts/resume.shEverything back (about 9 minutes when measured; the load balancer and WAF are recreated): waits until the services are healthy, then prints the HTTP status of the app. pause.sh sets PAUSED=true before the apply, resume.sh sets it to false after (needs gh logged in)
scripts/env-status.shRUNNING or PAUSED, resource by resource
Limits
AWS restarts a stopped RDS after 7 days (run pause.sh again). Starting a stopped RDS can fail briefly if AWS has no capacity in its zone: just try again. Costs are estimates from the price list, not the bill. terraform destroy gives zero cost. The full switch-on and switch-off cycle was tested for real: see "Standby until the presentation" at the end.

RDSSingle-AZ, storage autoscaling 20 → 50 GB, backups kept 1 day (free-plan cap), deletion protection off and no final snapshot, Postgres logs exported to CloudWatch (statements over 1 s)

Sign-up and social loginSelf sign-up is on (Terraform allow_self_signup, default true; e-mail verified; password policy of 12 characters). Google and Facebook sign-in go through Cognito identity providers, created only when google_client_id / facebook_app_id are set (secrets in the GitHub production environment). The production client never accepts a localhost redirect. In local mode (AUTH_MODE=local) the sign-up and social buttons go to a development login labelled as a simulation

Logs7 log groups (web, api, worker, scorer, migrate, sweeper, redteam), 30 days; ECR keeps the last 25 images and scans on push

Pipeline facts that matter

TopicFact
ConcurrencyPR runs cancel older runs of the same PR; main runs never cancel; the deploy has its own group and is never cancelled
Deploy jobRefuses to run while PAUSED=true; runs on an ARM runner; the PR docker-build runs on x86, only scans (Trivy, fixable HIGH and CRITICAL) and pushes nothing
Deploy permissionsBroad on purpose (ec2, ecs, rds, sqs, cloudfront, wafv2, cognito, secretsmanager, scheduler), but IAM only on quizforge-* roles and policies
TrustThe OIDC trust uses GitHub's immutable subject (owner and repo ids): a re-created repo with the same name cannot use the roles
ApprovalOne owner approves their own deploys (prevent_self_review is off); the ruleset needs 0 reviews but resolved threads and an up-to-date branch; squash merge only
SchedulesNightly eval at 05:43 UTC; drift check at 06:17 UTC (opens or updates one issue labelled drift); the red team on AWS at 06:00 UTC
Scannersgitleaks over the full history; Trivy over images and Terraform
ImagesECR holds api, worker, web and redteam. api, worker and redteam are tagged with the commit, web with web- + the front end commit; the scorer and sweeper use the worker image, the migration task the api image; tags are immutable
Bootstrap and GitHub stacksApplied by hand, not by the pipeline: changing the OIDC roles or the ruleset needs a local terraform apply
Test documentsServed from raw.githubusercontent.com/jhgcc1/quizforge/main/evals/fixtures, so the repository must stay public (or the files move to S3)

Limits and next steps

LimitDetail
No custom domainCloudFront → ALB is HTTP inside AWS (the ALB is locked to CloudFront). A domain + ACM certificate fixes it.
One NAT, single-AZ databaseA zone outage hurts. The db_multi_az flag exists.
TypeScript runs through tsxIn the api and worker/scorer images; a compiled build would start faster.
Similarity is lexical in productionTF-IDF catches near-duplicates, not paraphrases. Embeddings are used in the evals only.
Reference questionsDrafted by the AI; a human review is recommended.
No custom domain: TLS 1.0 and upCloudFront's default certificate cannot require TLS 1.2. A domain plus an ACM certificate fixes it.
Only 12 golden documentsSmall differences between variants are noise. English and Portuguese and Spanish.
Language detection is statisticalVery short or mixed texts can be misjudged; under 40 letters of prose the language is "unknown" and is let through.
Hidden-text guard is a heuristicIt blocks the techniques in the attack corpus and close variants; a new encoding is only stopped by the model's own resistance. See "Guardrails in execution".
Semantic detector recallLlama Prompt Guard 2 flags explicit attacks: 23.1% of the injections in the benchmark (25.8% in English), 0 false positives on the benign benchmark rows, 1 of 98 real READMEs flagged. It is one layer: it flags below 0.9 and refuses above it.
Only three languagesDocuments in any other language are rejected before the model; the keyword rules, the detector tests and the red-team sample are written for English, Portuguese and Spanish.
Alarm e-mailNothing is delivered until the AWS subscription e-mail has been confirmed.
Pause and resume scriptsThey pass the api image tag only (not the web tag) and do not read the social login secrets.
Audit scriptscripts/audit-aws.sh still expects admin-created users only in Cognito.
Nightly red teamThe first manual run found 2 leaked canaries: findings under investigation.

Ordered by area. Effort is a rough guess, not a plan.

Glossary

The words used in this page, in plain English.

WordPlain meaning
BFF (backend for frontend)The Next.js server that sits between the browser and the API. It holds the login cookie and adds the token.
PKCEA safe way to sign in with Cognito without a password ever reaching our code.
JWT / JWKSThe signed login token, and the public keys the API uses to check the signature.
SQS · dead-letter queue (DLQ)A message queue. A message that fails 3 times moves to the DLQ and raises an alarm.
Visibility timeoutHow long a message stays hidden while a worker handles it. If the worker dies, it comes back.
Idempotency keyA random id the browser sends once per action, so a retry never creates a second quiz.
Lease + row lockHow two scorers avoid judging the same quiz at once.
CheckpointThe agent's progress saved in Postgres after each step, so a restart continues instead of starting again. It is deleted when the quiz is saved, and after 24 hours at the latest.
LLM judgeA second model call that grades the quiz. It is noisy, so we take the median of 3.
EMFA log line format that CloudWatch turns into a metric, which alarms can watch.
OTLPThe standard way our code sends traces to Langfuse.
SSRF guardChecks that stop the README URL from pointing to private or internal addresses.
promptfooA test runner for prompts and AI behaviour. Here it runs the real pipeline against an attack corpus (offline on every PR; live on a PR when relevant, on main and nightly).
Red teamAttacking your own system on purpose to find a leak. Here: 50 frozen attacks in English, Portuguese and Spanish, run in CI on every pull request, and a fresh larger set every night on AWS.
FlagWhat Prompt Guard 2 does below the refusal threshold: it marks the most suspicious window and records it (log, metric), and the document is generated — under stricter output rails. At 0.9 or above it refuses instead.
ExcerptThe first 80 characters of the window of the document that Prompt Guard 2 scored highest.
Strict link modeWhen the document has a flag, the output rail accepts a link only if it occurs in the document without the flagged parts, and rejects a link with a word found only in them.
Deploy, scope webThe manual workflow of the infrastructure repository deploying only the front end, at the newest green commit of its main.
RollbackThe separate workflow that goes back to a named image tag. The only place where a tag is typed by hand; the database migration is not undone.
CanaryA made-up token (for example ZX9-ALPHA) that appears in an attack and in no honest quiz. If it shows up in a reply, the attack worked.
Prompt Guard 2Llama Prompt Guard 2 86M: Meta's small model that tells a prompt injection from a normal text. It flags a document below 0.9 and refuses it above, which is the one refusal a user can appeal (see the review flow).
Semantic detectorThe part of the worker that runs the Prompt Guard 2 model on the document text (packages/detector).
Contract (@quizforge/contract)The zod schemas of what goes in and out of the API, released as a tarball that the front end repository depends on.
apply.ymlThe reusable workflow of the infrastructure repository with the production path: approval, drift check, migration, apply, smoke tests. Called by both Deploy and Rollback.
Block, flag, sanitizeThe three outcomes of the input guard: reject the document, keep it as data and count it, or clean it.
Output railsCode (no second model) that checks what the model returned: JSON only, no prompt leak, no script or new links, no echoed attack, really questions.
HomoglyphA letter from another alphabet that looks like a Latin one (Cyrillic “а” for “a”), used to hide a word from a filter.
ROT13, Base64, hexWays to write text so a person cannot read it at a glance. The guard decodes them and looks inside.
Zero-width / tag charactersCharacters that take no space on screen. They can carry a hidden message, so they are removed or rejected.
zod (the Node “Pydantic”)A schema library: one definition is both the TypeScript type and the runtime check.
Expand / contract migrationDatabase changes made in two safe steps, so old and new code both keep working during a deploy.

Standby until the presentation

How to spend almost nothing until the day everything must run on AWS, and the test that proves the switch on and off works.

The idea

Keep the AWS part in standby (about US$0.3 a day) and switch it on only for the days when everything must run: the final tests and the presentation. The cycle was run for real on 2026-10-10 (resume, check, pause again) and it found one bug (below).

The procedure

StepCommandWhat happensMeasured
Standbyscripts/env-status.shShows PAUSED: tasks at 0, RDS stopped, no NAT, no load balancer, no WAF—
Switch onAWS_PROFILE=... scripts/resume.shCreates the NAT, load balancer and WAF, starts the database, scales the 4 services up, waits until healthy, prints the HTTP status of the app8 min 54 s (app answered 200 on / and /openapi.json)
Deploy the current codeApprove the production deploy on the latest run of main (it refuses to run while PAUSED=true; resume.sh sets it to false)Builds the images of the commit, runs the migration, rolls the services, smoke testPipeline time (not part of this test)
Switch offAWS_PROFILE=... scripts/pause.shCloudFront lets go of the WAF and the load balancer, then tasks to 0, WAF and load balancer deleted, NAT removed, RDS stopped, sweeper off2 min 5 s

Checks done after each step

AfterCheckResult
Resumeterraform plan with paused=falseNo changes (no drift)
ResumeApp through CloudFront: /, /openapi.json, /v1/quizzes without a token200, 200, 401 (the API answers and still asks for a login)
ResumeResourcesweb 2, api 2, worker 1, scorer 1 running · RDS available · NAT, load balancer and WAF present · sweeper enabled
Pausescripts/env-status.shAll services 0 · RDS stopped · no NAT · no load balancer · sweeper disabled · PAUSED
Pauseterraform plan with paused=trueNo changes
PauseWAF web ACLs in the account, and the CloudFront WebACLId0 and empty: the WAF is really gone, CloudFront is still there
Next resumeterraform plan with paused=false8 to add, 9 to change, 1 to destroy: the same numbers as the real resume

The bug the test found

Pausing failed with WAFAssociatedItemException
Terraform tried to delete the WAF while CloudFront still used it, and AWS refuses that. Terraform does not put “update the distribution” before “delete the web ACL” when the web ACL disappears with count = 0. The apply stopped half-way (load balancer and NAT already gone, tasks still up). Fix: pause.sh runs two applies. Phase 1 (-target the distribution, keep_waf=true) only updates CloudFront so it releases the WAF and the load balancer. Phase 2 deletes the rest. Resume needed no change: creating things in order is what Terraform does well.

Files

FileRole
scripts/pause.shThe two-phase pause (the fix); sets PAUSED=true
scripts/resume.shThe resume and the health wait; sets PAUSED=false
scripts/env-status.shOne-screen status: RUNNING or PAUSED, resource by resource
scripts/_env.shShared helpers: Terraform init, the deployed image tag, running tasks, the PAUSED variable
quizforge-infra: terraform/pause.tfThe paused flag: what is stopped, and the RDS start/stop
quizforge-infra: terraform/edge.tfLoad balancer and WAF (count follows paused), the CloudFront distribution, the keep_waf switch
quizforge-infra: terraform/variables.tfVariables paused and keep_waf
quizforge-infra: terraform/network.tfThe NAT gateway and its address (removed while paused)
.github/workflows/ci.ymlThe deploy job refuses to run while PAUSED=true
Before the presentation
Resume at least one hour before (9 minutes for the stack, plus the deploy and the smoke test). After it, run pause.sh the same day. If you stay paused for more than 7 days, run pause.sh again, because AWS restarts a stopped RDS by itself.
